name: InterAgentMessage
summary: A message from one agent to another, where the direction is the data.

a11y.apg: disclosure — the reason is a native <details>, so opening and closing is the platform's. The from/to pair is a named group: the arrow is an Icon and Icons are always aria-hidden, so without the name a screen reader would hear two names side by side and lose the direction, which is the whole point of this component.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: Enter, which opens the message's detail. The detail is a native <details>/<summary>, the same idiom as the Accordion, so the keyboard is the platform's. Space is DECLARED and did NOT toggle it: measured directly on 29/08/2026 by reading the open attribute before and after the key, in Chromium build 1194. It stays declared because activating a summary with Space is the documented HTML behaviour and other engines do deliver it — what is recorded here is that this build did not.

props.name: messages
props.description: Each entry carries from, to, body and an optional kind. Not MessageList: that one is a conversation with a person; here the handoff between two agents is what you are reading, and a list with two authors cannot say who delivered what to whom.

notes: `to` is optional: a broadcast has no single target, and the component says so in words rather than leaving the field blank.

The six colours by intent from the reference (technical cyan, billing amber, sales slate…) did NOT come in. It is the third time Part H refuses the same thing — after the eleven span colours in H.d and the six state colours in H.a. Colour by category inside a locked palette is unreadable for anyone who does not separate colours; kind enters as a word, in a badge.
